﴿رَمى﴾: the clause is the khabar of لكن. ﴿وَلِيُبْلِيَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, i.e. "فعل الله هذا" (Allah did this).. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ, a sound masculine plural. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from بلاء. ﴿بَلاءً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and ﴿حَسَناً﴾ is a ṣifa (adjective). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾: inna, its noun and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿ذلِكُمْ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "ذلكم حق" (that is the truth); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ﴾: anna, the Name of Majesty its noun and موهن its khabar. ﴿كَيْدِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْكافِرِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ in place of the kasra, a sound masculine plural. أن with its noun and its khabar is, by interpretation, a maṣdar (verbal noun) conjoined to what precedes it, i.e. "ذلكم حق وتوهين كيد الكافرين حق" (that is the truth, and the weakening of the plotting of the disbelievers is the truth)..

daas-irab:19-19.t:
﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿تَسْتَفْتِحُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿فَقَدْ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ﴾: a past verb, its mafʿūl (object) and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and likewise وإن ﴿تَنْتَهُوا﴾. ﴿فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ﴾: the clause is in the position of [the jussive as] the apodosis. «[Translator's note: the word "jussive" (جزم) is missing in the source.]» ﴿وَإِنْ تَعُودُوا﴾: its i'rab is like the preceding. ﴿نَعُدْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis. ﴿وَلَنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لن governs the subjunctive. ﴿تُغْنِيَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾ are attached (mutaʿalliq). ﴿فِئَتُكُمْ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾: a substitute for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), or mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
لو is a non-jussive conditional. ﴿كَثُرَتْ﴾: a past verb; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the adverb ﴿مَعَ﴾ is attached to its omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). أن with its noun and its khabar is, by interpretation, a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, i.e. "ولأن الله مع المؤمنين" (and because Allah is with the believers).

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: for its i'rab see verse 15. ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾: see the first verse. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and لا is the prohibitive لا, governing the jussive. ﴿تَوَلَّوْا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تولوا; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). And the clause ﴿تَسْمَعُونَ﴾ is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate). The nominal clause وأنتم تسمعون is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿وَلا﴾: the prohibitive لا, governing the jussive, and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿تَكُونُوا﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as its noun. ﴿كَالَّذِينَ﴾: the kāf is a preposition, and the relative noun is in the position of the genitive governed by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); or the kāf is a noun meaning "like" (مثل), which is the khabar, and the relative noun is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). The verbal clause ﴿قالُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَهُمْ لا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾: like His saying, the Exalted, وأنتم تسمعون in the previous verse.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿إِنَّ شَرَّ﴾: inna and its noun. ﴿الدَّوَابِّ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the elative (ism al-tafḍīl) شر. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿الصُّمُّ﴾: first khabar (predicate). ﴿الْبُكْمُ﴾: second khabar. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as a ṣifa (adjective), and the clause ﴿لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. The nominal clause إن شر.. is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle, and the wāw is resumptive. ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached (mutaʿalliq), and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿خَيْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the lām occurs in the apodosis, and the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition; and the clause ﴿وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ﴾ is conjoined. ﴿لَتَوَلَّوْا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the lām likewise links the apodosis. The nominal clause ﴿وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:24-24.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: see verse 15. ﴿اسْتَجِيبُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَلِلرَّسُولِ﴾: conjoined. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb attached to استجيبوا, and the clause استجيبوا is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿دَعاكُمْ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied on the alif; its fāʿil is "هو" and the kāf its mafʿūl (object). The clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿لِما﴾: the lām is a preposition; ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive governed by the lām. The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to دعاكم. ما may also be parsed as maṣdariyya. ﴿يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ because of heaviness; its fāʿil is "هو", the kāf is its mafʿūl, and the mīm is for the masculine plural. The clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: like استجيبوا, and it is conjoined to it. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause ﴿يَحُولُ﴾ is its khabar (predicate). ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb attached to يحول. ﴿الْمَرْءِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَقَلْبِهِ﴾: conjoined. The interpreted maṣdar formed from أن, its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of علم. ﴿وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾: the second interpreted maṣdar is conjoined. And ﴿إِلَيْهِ﴾ is attached to the verb ﴿تُحْشَرُونَ﴾. The clause تحشرون is the khabar.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to استجيبوا. ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لا تُصِيبَنَّ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and لا is negating with no governing effect. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ṣifa (adjective). ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿خَاصَّةً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: conjoined to اتقوا. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن, its noun and its khabar (predicate) stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿الْعِقابِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:26-26.t:
﴿وَاذْكُرُوا﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb for past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿قَلِيلٌ﴾: first khabar (predicate). ﴿مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ﴾: second khabar, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to مستضعفون. ﴿تَخافُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is a third khabar. ﴿أَنْ يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿النَّاسُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿فَآواكُمْ﴾: آوى is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied on the alif, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَأَيَّدَكُمْ بِنَصْرِهِ﴾: a past verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; the fāʿil is "هو" and the kāf its mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّباتِ﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾: laʿalla, and the kāf is its noun, and the clause ﴿تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ is its khabar. The clause لعلكم is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-27.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: it has preceded in verse 15. ﴿لا تَخُونُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and ﴿اللَّهَ﴾, the Name of Majesty, is its mafʿūl (object). ﴿وَالرَّسُولَ﴾: conjoined.
﴿تَخُونُوا﴾: conjoined to the first تخونوا; or the wāw is the wāw of accompaniment (maʿiyya), and تخونوا is accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the wāw of accompaniment, the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn. ﴿أَماناتِكُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of its accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa.
The kāf is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). And the nominal clause ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial)..

daas-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾:
the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّما﴾:
the restraining particle and the restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَمْوالُكُمْ﴾:
mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿وَأَوْلادُكُمْ﴾:
conjoined. ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾:
khabar (predicate); the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾:
anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿عِنْدَهُ﴾:
an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar. ﴿أَجْرٌ﴾:
a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of أن. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾:
ṣifa (adjective). The clause اعلموا is conjoined.

daas-irab:29-29.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional. ﴿تَتَّقُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يَجْعَلْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يجعل. ﴿فُرْقاناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيُكَفِّرْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to the apodosis; the accusative is also permissible in it, by an implied أن,
and the nominative as a resumption. ﴿عَنْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سَيِّئاتِكُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural; the kāf is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa); the clause is conjoined. And likewise the clause ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ذُو﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿الْفَضْلِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْعَظِيمِ﴾: ṣifa (adjective); the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:30-30.t:
﴿وَإِذْ﴾: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted verb اذكر (remember); the clause is conjoined. ﴿يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾: an imperfect verb to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached, and the relative noun after it is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). And the clause ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿لِيُثْبِتُوكَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb يمكر. ﴿أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَيَمْكُرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ﴾: the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ﴾: the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير its khabar (predicate). ﴿الْماكِرِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:31-31.t:
﴿وَإِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, containing the meaning of condition. ﴿تُتْلى﴾: an imperfect verb in the passive, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif because of impossibility. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿آياتُنا﴾ «[Translator's note: the opening bracket of this word is missing in the source.]»: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). The clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation.
﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is "نحن"; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَقُلْنا﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis. ﴿قلنا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿مِثْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative. ﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿إِنْ﴾: negating. ﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَساطِيرُ﴾: khabar (predicate). ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

daas-irab:32-32.t:
﴿وَإِذْ﴾: conjoined to the previous verses. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿اللَّهُمَّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a single proper noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of the accusative; the doubled mīm replaces the omitted vocative yāʾ. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿هذا﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as its noun.
﴿هُوَ﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾: khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from الحق; the clause is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَأَمْطِرْ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and a verb of supplication to which the preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ are attached; its fāʿil is "أنت". ﴿حِجارَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of حجارة; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿أَوِ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿ائْتِنا﴾: a verb of supplication, indeclinable on the deletion of the weak letter, the yāʾ; نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". ﴿بِعَذابٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَلِيمٍ﴾: ṣifa; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:33-33.t: ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: negating. ﴿كانَ اللَّهُ﴾: kāna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of denial (lām al-juḥūd); the hāʾ is its mafʿūl (object), and the mīm is for the masculine plural. The interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿وَأَنْتَ﴾: a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾: the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl, and the clause ﴿يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ is the khabar.

daas-irab:34-34.t:
﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿إِنْ﴾: a particle governing the subjunctive. «[Translator's note: so in the source, "إن"; the particle in the verse is أَلَّا, i.e. أنْ + لا.]» ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿يُعَذِّبَهُمُ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl (object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive governed by a preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent). ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ, and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿يَصُدُّونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْحَرامِ﴾: ṣifa (adjective). The verbal clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial, and ما is negating. ﴿كانُوا أَوْلِياءَهُ﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿إِنْ﴾: negating. ﴿أَوْلِياؤُهُ﴾: mubtadaʾ, nominative by the ḍamma, and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). «[Translator's note: so in the source, written ﴿أَلَّا﴾; the word in the verse is إِلَّا.]» ﴿الْمُتَّقُونَ﴾: khabar, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿أَكْثَرَهُمْ﴾: its noun. ﴿لا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; لا is negating; the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar of لكن, and the nominal clause ولكن أكثرهم.. is circumstantial.

daas-irab:35-35.t:
﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a particle of resumption; ما is negating. ﴿كانَ صَلاتُهُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from صلاتهم. ﴿الْبَيْتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿مُكاءً﴾: khabar (predicate). ﴿وَتَصْدِيَةً﴾: conjoined.
﴿فَذُوقُوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition). ﴿ذوقوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾: its mafʿūl (object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition and ما is maṣdariyya. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾: kāna, the tāʾ is its noun and the mīm for the masculine plural; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the incomplete verb and the verb after it with the maṣdariyya ما is in the position of the genitive governed by the bāʾ, i.e. "because of your disbelief". The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb ذوقوا, and the clause ﴿تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ is the khabar.

daas-irab:36-36.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾: inna and its noun, and the clause ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; the clause إن الذين is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوالَهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl (object); the clause is in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿لِيَصُدُّوا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb ينفقون. ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يصدوا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَسَيُنْفِقُونَها﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of resumption. ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is its mafʿūl; the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿ثُمَّ تَكُونُ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, its noun a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to الأموال (the wealth). ﴿حَسْرَةً﴾: its khabar. The preposition and its genitive noun ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from حسرة, because it comes after it «[Translator's note: so in the source; عليهم actually follows حسرة in the verse.]»; the clause is conjoined, and likewise the clause ﴿ثُمَّ يُغْلَبُونَ﴾ is conjoined. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾: conjoined to الذين at the beginning of the verse. ﴿إِلى جَهَنَّمَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb يحشرون. جهنم is genitive by the fatḥa in place of the kasra, because of being a proper noun and foreign; and the clause ﴿يُحْشَرُونَ﴾ is the khabar.

daas-irab:37-37.t: ﴿لِيَمِيزَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive governed by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb يغلبون. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent). ﴿الْخَبِيثَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الخبيث. ﴿وَيَجْعَلَ الْخَبِيثَ﴾: conjoined. ﴿بَعْضَهُ﴾: badal (substitute), accusative. ﴿عَلى بَعْضٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from بعضه. ﴿فَيَرْكُمَهُ﴾: conjoined to يجعل. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾: ḥāl. ﴿فَيَجْعَلَهُ﴾: conjoined. ﴿فِي جَهَنَّمَ﴾: a noun, genitive (majrūr) by the fatḥa; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿هُمُ﴾: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْخاسِرُونَ﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

daas-irab:38-38.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنْ﴾: a jussive particle. ﴿يَنْتَهُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿يُغْفَرْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the passive, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the verbal clause قد سلف is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَإِنْ يَعُودُوا﴾: like إن ينتهوا..; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and a past verb and fāʿil. ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis.

daas-irab:39-39.t:
﴿وَقاتِلُوهُمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm is for the masculine plural. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit (ghāya) and a preposition. ﴿لا﴾: negating. ﴿تَكُونَ﴾: a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb meaning "occur" (تقع), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the genitive governed by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb قاتلوهم. ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾: fāʿil; and the clause قاتلوهم is conjoined to the clause قل..
﴿وَيَكُونَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb. ﴿الدِّينُ﴾: its noun. ﴿كُلُّهُ﴾: tawkīd (emphasis), nominative. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of the incomplete verb; the clause is conjoined.
﴿فَإِنِ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive. ﴿إن﴾: a conditional particle. ﴿انْتَهَوْا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
﴿فَإِنِ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and إن is a particle resembling the verb. «[Translator's note: so in the source, written ﴿فَإِنِ﴾; the word in the verse is فَإِنَّ.]» ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Name of Majesty, its noun. ﴿بِما﴾: ما is maṣdariyya or a relative, in the position of the genitive governed by the preposition. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar, taking ما as maṣdariyya, is in the position of the genitive governed by the preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the khabar. ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾: khabar.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا رَمَيْتَ إِذْ رَمَيْتَ وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَمَىٰ﴾: on the day of Badr the Messenger of Allah ﷺ called for a handful of dust and threw it into the faces of the people, saying: "شاهت الوجوه" ("May the faces be disfigured"), that is, may they be made ugly; and that too was a cause of their rout.

farraa:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾, and also (موَهِّن). If you wish you put it in iḍāfa (genitive construct), and if you wish you give it tanwīn (nunation) and put [the following noun] in the accusative. Like it are (إنّ اللّهَ بَالِغُ أمْرِهِ، وبَالغٌ أمْرَهُ) and (كاشفاتُ ضُرِّه، وكاشِفَاتٌ ضُرَّه).

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾: Abū Jahl said on that day: "O Allah, give victory to the better of the two religions and the one more deserving of victory." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِن تَسْتَفْتِحُواْ فَقَدْ جَآءَكُمُ ٱلْفَتْحُ﴾, meaning victory.
His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: he said: putting a kasra on its alif (i.e. reading إِنَّ) is dearer to me than putting a fatḥa on it, because in the reading of ʿAbdallāh [ibn Masʿūd] it is (وإن الله لمع المؤمنين), and this makes the kasra good, as the beginning of a new sentence. Whoever gives it a fatḥa connects it with ﴿وَلَن تُغْنِيَ عَنْكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ شَيْئاً وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ﴾, meaning: "because of its great number and because Allah is with the believers"; so its position is accusative (naṣb), since the genitive (khafḍ) [i.e. an implied preposition] is suitable in it.

farraa:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿وَٱتَّقُواْ فِتْنَةً لاَّ تُصِيبَنَّ﴾: He commanded them and then forbade them, and there is in it a touch of the jazāʾ (conditional apodosis), even though it is a prohibition. Like it is His saying ﴿يأيها النمل ادخلوا مساكِنكم لا يحطِمنَّكم﴾: she commanded them and then forbade them, and there is in it the sense of the jazāʾ.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱذْكُرُوۤاْ إِذْ أَنتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُّسْتَضْعَفُونَ﴾ was revealed about the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn) specifically.
His saying: ﴿فَآوَاكُمْ﴾ means: to Medina; ﴿وَأَيَّدَكُم بِنَصْرِهِ﴾ means: He strengthened you.

farraa:27-27.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ تَخُونُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ وَتَخُونُوۤاْ أَمَانَاتِكُمْ﴾: if you wish you make it jussive (jazm) as a prohibition, and if you wish you make it ṣarf (the "turning-away" construction) and put it in the accusative. [The poet] said:
لا تنه عن خُلُقٍ وتأتِىَ مِثلَه * عار عليك إِذا فعلت عظيم
(Do not forbid a trait while you yourself do its like; a great shame upon you if you do.)
And in one of the two readings it is (ولا تخونوا أماناتِكم), so here too it may be jussive or accusative.

farraa:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿إَن تَتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّكُمْ فُرْقَاناً﴾: He says: an opening (victory) and help. Likewise His saying ﴿يوم الفرقانِ يوم التقى الجمعانِ﴾: the day of the opening and of victory.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِيُثْبِتُوكَ أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾: a group of Quraysh gathered and said: "What is your view about Muḥammad ﷺ?" Iblīs came in among them in the form of a man from the people of Najd. ʿAmr ibn Hishām said: "My view is that you confine him in a house, plaster it up over him, open a small window for him and press hard on him until he dies." Iblīs rejected that and said: "What a bad opinion your opinion is!" Abū al-Bakhtarī ibn Hishām said: "My view is that he be put on a camel and then driven off with it until he perishes, or some of the Arabs rid you of him." Iblīs said: "What a bad opinion! Would you send away from yourselves a man who has corrupted most of you, so that he falls in with others than you? Perhaps he would then raid you with them." The wicked one, Abū Jahl, said: "My view is that we go to him with a man from every clan of Quraysh and strike him with our swords." Iblīs said: "The right opinion is what this young man has given." Jibrīl, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ with the news, and he left Mecca, he and Abū Bakr. So His saying (ليثبتوك) means: to confine you in the house; (أو يخرِجوك): on the camel; (أو يقتلوك).
[Translator's note: the source writes «صى الله عليه وسلم», evidently a misprint for «صلى الله عليه وسلم»; rendered as ﷺ.]

farraa:32-32.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالُواْ ٱللَّهُمَّ إِن كَانَ هَـٰذَا هُوَ ٱلْحَقَّ مِنْ عِندِكَ﴾: in (الحق) there is the accusative and the nominative. If you make (هو) a noun [i.e. a mubtadaʾ (subject)], you put الحق in the nominative by هو. If you make it an ʿimād (support pronoun; the Kufan term for the separating pronoun), functioning like a ṣila (redundant link), you put الحق in the accusative. Do the same with the sisters of kāna, and with aẓunnu (I think) and its sisters, as Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, said: ﴿ويرى الذِين أوتو العِلم الذى أنزِل إليك مِن ربك هو الحق﴾: you put الحق in the accusative because (رأيت) is one of the sisters of ẓanantu. Every place where yafʿalu or faʿala would be suitable in place of the accusative "fiʿl" [i.e. the predicate] admits the ʿimād and the accusative of that "fiʿl"; and it also admits its nominative by هو, if you make it a noun. And the alif and lām (the definite article) are indispensable when you find a way to them. So if you say: وجدت عبدالله هو خيرا منك وشرا منك أو أفضل منك ("I found ʿAbdallāh better than you / worse than you / more excellent than you"), then in whatever resembles this "fiʿl" there is both accusative and nominative: the accusative on the basis that the alif and lām are intended, even if they cannot be inserted; and the nominative on the basis that you make (هو) a noun. So you say: ظننت أخاك هو أصغُر منك and هو أصغرَ منك ("I thought your brother younger than you").
When you come to proper nouns such as ʿAmr and Muḥammad, or to nouns in iḍāfa such as أبيك (your father) and أخيك (your brother), you put them in the nominative, saying: أظنّ زيدا هو أخوك and أظنّ أخاك هو زيد, putting it in the nominative, since you have not brought the sign of the "returned" element (al-mardūd) but have brought هو, which is the sign of the noun. The sign of the "returned" element is that every "fiʿl" which has no alif and lām is brought back with alif and lām and refers back to the noun; so (هو) is a support for the noun and (the alif and lām) a support for the "fiʿl". Since the alif and lām could not be supplied, and it was not proper to intend them in زيد, because it is a [proper] name, nor in الأخ, because it is in iḍāfa, they preferred the nominative. It is proper in (أفضل منك) because you drop (من) and say: رأيتك أنت الأفضل ("I saw you to be the most excellent"); but it is not proper in (زيد) or in (الأخ) to intend an alif and lām. Al-Kisāʾī used to allow it, saying: رأيت أخاك هو زيدا and رأيت زيدا هو أخاك. And it is permissible, just as it was permissible in (أفضل) because of the intention, the intention of the alif and lām; and likewise it was permissible in زيد and أخيك. When the alif and lām are possible for you and yet you do not bring them, use the nominative; so you say: رأيت زيدا هو قائم and رأيت عمرا هو جالس.
The poet said:
إجِدَّك لن تزال نجِىَّ هَمّ * تبيت الليل أنت له ضجيع
(Is it in earnest that you will never cease to be the confidant of care, spending the night as its bedfellow?)
And the accusative is permissible in (ليت) by way of the ʿimād, and the nominative for one who says: ليتك قائما. Al-Kisāʾī recited to me:
ليت الشباب هو الرجيع على الفتى * والشيب كان هو البدئُ الأوّل
(Would that youth were what returns to a young man, and grey hair were the first beginning.)
He used the accusative with (ليت) by way of the ʿimād and the nominative with كان by way of the noun. Definite and indefinite are the same in this.

farraa:41-41.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱعْلَمُوۤا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ للَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾: (أَنَّ) came both at its beginning and its end because it is a jazāʾ (conditional), like His saying ﴿كُتِبَ عليه أَنه مَنْ تَولاَّهُ فأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّه﴾ and like His saying ﴿أَلم يَعْلَمُوا أَنه مَنْ يحادِدِ اللَّه ورسولَه فأَنَّ له نارَ جهنَّم﴾. It is permissible in the second (أنّ) to give its alif a kasra, because its dropping is permissible: do you not see that if you said (اعلموا أنّ ما غنمتم من شىء فللّه خمسه) it would be sound? So since its dropping is sound, one gives it a kasra.
His saying: ﴿وَلِذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾: the kinsfolk of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾: the orphans and the poor of the people [at large]; the orphans and the poor of Banū Hāshim are not included in it.

farraa:42-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ أَنتُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾: al-ʿudwa is the bank of the valley; (الدينا) [i.e. الدنيا, "the nearer"] is the side next to Medina, and (القصوى) ("the farther") the side next to Mecca.
[Translator's note: the source prints «الدينا», apparently a misprint for «الدنيا».]
His saying ﴿وَٱلرَّكْبُ أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ means Abū Sufyān and the caravan; they were on the seashore.
His saying ﴿أَسْفَلَ مِنكُمْ﴾ is accusative; it means: a place lower than you. Had He described them as being low, meaning "and the caravan were lower", it would have been permissible, in the nominative.
His saying: ﴿وَيَحْيَىٰ مَنْ حَيَّ عَن بَيِّنَةٍ﴾: it is written with idghām (assimilation), with a single yāʾ, and that is the reading of most of the readers. Some of them read (حَيىَِ عن بيّنة) with the two made distinct. They assimilated the yāʾ into the yāʾ, though they ought not to have done so, because the second yāʾ is bound to take the fatḥa in faʿala; they assimilated because two vowelled letters of the same kind met. Assimilation is permissible in the dual because of the fixed vowel of the last yāʾ, so you say of two men: قد حَيّا and حَيِيا. In the plural one ought not to assimilate, because its yāʾ would receive the ḍamma while what precedes it has a kasra, so it ought to become quiescent and drop before the wāw of the plural. Yet sometimes the Arabs have used assimilation in the plural, aiming at making the verb forms uniform and having them all doubled.
So they said for حَيِيت: حَيُّوا, and for عيِيت: عَيُّوا. One of them recited to me:
يَحِدن بِنا عن كلّ حَىٍّ كأننا * أخاريس عَيُّوا بالسلام وبالنَّسْبِ
(They [the camels] veer with us away from every tribe, as though we were mutes who could manage neither greeting nor lineage.)
He means النّسَب. Another said:
مِن الذين إذا قلنا: حَدِيثَكم * عَيُّوا، وإن نحن حَدَّثناهُمُ شَغِبَوا
(Of those who, when we say "Your story!", are tongue-tied, and when we talk to them, make an uproar.)
The Arabs are agreed on assimilating التحيّة and التحيّات because of the vowel of the last yāʾ in them, just as they favoured assimilating عىَّ and حَىَّ because of the fixed vowel in them. It may also be correct to assimilate yāʾ into yāʾ in يَحْيا and يَعْيا, though this is rarer than the assimilation in حىّ, because the yāʾ of يحيا is quiescent when it is in the nominative position, so the vowel in it is not fixed. Its justification is that when you put it in the accusative, as in the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, ﴿أَليس ذلِك بِقادِرٍ على أَن يُحْيِىَ المَوْتَى﴾, assimilation is correct there; then you make the speech uniform, so that it has assimilation in the nominative and the jussive too; and you say (هو يُحِىُّ ويُمِيت). One of them recited to me:
وكأنها بين النساءِ سبِيكةٌ * تمشى بِسُدَّةِ بَيْتها فَتُعِىُّ
(As if she, among the women, were an ingot [of gold]; she walks to the threshold of her house and grows weary.)
And likewise يَحَيَّان and يَحَيُّون.

farraa:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَانُ أَعْمَالَهُمْ وَقَالَ لاَ غَالِبَ لَكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ﴾: this is Iblīs, who appeared in the form of a man of Banū Kināna called Surāqa ibn Juʿshum. Al-Farrāʾ said: His saying ﴿وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَّكُمْ﴾ means: [your protector] against my people, Banū Kināna, so that they do not interfere with you, and so that they will be with you against Muḥammad ﷺ. When he saw the angels he recognised them, so "he turned back on his heels" (نَكَصَ على عَقِبَيْه). Al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām said to him: "O Surāqa, fleeing without a fight?!" He said: (إنى أَرَى ما لا تَرَوْن) ("I see what you do not see").

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿يَضْرِبُونَ وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ وَذُوقُواْ﴾ means: "and they say", implied (muḍmar), as He said: ﴿ولَوْ تَرَى إذِ المُجْرِمُونَ نَاكِسُو رُءُوسِهم عِنْدَ رَبِّهِم رَبَّنَا﴾, meaning: they say: (رَبَّنا). And in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: ﴿وَإِذْ يرفع إِبراهِيمُ القواعِدَ من البيتِ وإِسماعيلُ﴾ "the two of them saying" ﴿رَبَّنا﴾.

farraa:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلاَّمٍ لِّلْعَبِيدِ﴾: (أَنّ) is in the position of the accusative if you make (ذلك) accusative and mean: We did ﴿ذٰلِكَ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ and because ﴿أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾. If you wish, you make (ذلك) in the position of the nominative, and then you make (أنْ) in the position of the nominative, as you say: هذا ذاك ("this is that").

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ means: these denied just as the family of Pharaoh denied, so there befell them what befell the family of Pharaoh.

farraa:57-57.t:
His saying: ﴿فَإِمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِي ٱلْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ بِهِم مَّنْ خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ means: if you take them captive, O Muḥammad, then make an example of them to those behind them, those whom you fear will break the covenant: ﴿فَشرِّدْ بِهِمْ﴾.
﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾: so that they do not break the covenant. It has sometimes been read (مِن خَلْفِهِم), with a kasra on (مِن), but it has no meaning that I approve of in view of the exegesis.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِن قَوْمٍ خِيَانَةً﴾: He says: breaking of a covenant; ﴿فَٱنْبِذْ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ with the breaking [i.e. throw back the treaty to them], ﴿عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾: He says: do as they do, equally. It is also said about His saying ﴿عَلَىٰ سَوَآءٍ﴾: openly, not in secret. His saying ﴿تَخافَنّ﴾ is in the position of the jussive. The Arabs hardly ever put the heavy or the light nūn [of emphasis] in a jazāʾ (conditional) until they join it to (ما); and when they join it, they prefer the nūn. That is because they found that (إمّا), when it is conditional, resembles the (إمّا) of choice ("either… or"), so they introduced the nūn so that the difference between the two might be known by it. Then they made most of its apodoses with fāʾ; thus the Revelation came. He said: ﴿فَإمَّا تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ فِى الحربِ فشَرِّد﴾, and ﴿فإمّا نُرِيَنَّك بعض الذِى نَعِدهم﴾, then He said ﴿فإلينا يرجعون﴾. The fāʾ was chosen because when they put the nūn with (إمّا) they make it the head of the sentence and hardly ever postpone it. It is not their usage to say: اضربه إمّا يقومَنَّ ("Hit him if he stands up"); their usage is to put it first. Since it was bound to come first, it became like something outside the condition, so they favoured the fāʾ with it and preferred it, just as they favoured it in their saying أمّا أخوكم فقاعد ("As for your brother, he is sitting"), since it resembles that.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «فاسحبوا», apparently a misprint for «فاستحبّوا» ("they favoured"); translated in that sense.]

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ سَبَقُوۤاْ إِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُعْجِزُونَ﴾ is with tāʾ (تحسبنّ), there being no disagreement about it. But Ḥamza read it with yāʾ; and we think he took it in light of the reading of ʿAbdallāh.
In the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا إنهم لا يُعْجِزون). If (أنّهم) is not in it, it is not right for the verb of thinking (ẓann) not to fall on anything [as its object]. Had he meant: "Let not those who disbelieve think that they cannot be frustrated", it would be right, making لا a ṣila (redundant), as in His saying: ﴿وحَرامٌ على قَرْيةٍ أَهلكناها أَنّهم لا يَرْجِعون﴾, meaning: that they will return. And if (أنْ) were with (سبقوا) it would be right, so that you say (ولا يحسب الذين كفروا أن سبقوا).
If someone says: "Is it not Arab usage to say عسيت أذهب ('maybe I shall go') and أريد أقوم معك ('I want to stand with you'), with (أنْ) implied in both? So why is it not permissible to say أظن أقوم ('I think I shall stand') and أظن قمت ('I think I stood')?" I reply: if that were done with ẓanantu when the verb belongs to the one mentioned [i.e. the subject], I would allow it, even if it is a noun, as in their saying: عسى الغُوَيْرُ أَبْؤُساً ("perhaps the little cave holds misfortunes"), the proper form being with أنْ. If you say that, you would say it with aẓunnu too, saying أظن أقوم and أظن قمت, because the verb is yours. But it is not permissible to say أظن يقوم زيد, nor عسيت يقوم زيد, nor أردت يقوم زيد. It is permissible when the verb belongs to him [the subject] because, when you turn yafʿalu into fāʿil (the active participle), it is joined to it and is accusative by its owner; so one says أريد قائما ("I want [to be] standing"), the standing being yours. You do not say أريد قائما زيد; and whoever says this says the like with ẓanantu. One of them recited to me, by Dhū al-Rumma:
أَظَنَّ ابْنُ طُرْثوثِ عُتَيْبةُ ذاهبا * بعادِيَّتِى تَكْذابُه وَجعائِلُهْ
(Did Ibn Ṭurthūth, ʿUtayba, think his lying and his bribes would make off with my wronging?)
So this is a line of reasoning for the reading of Ḥamza: he makes (سبقوا) in the position of the accusative: "Let not those who disbelieve think [themselves] outstripping (sābiqīn)." But I do not like it, because it is anomalous.
[Translator's note: the opening statement that the tāʾ reading has "no disagreement" and then that Ḥamza read with yāʾ is translated as written; it seems to mean that the tāʾ reading is the agreed reading of the majority. The poetic gloss is tentative.]

farraa:60-60.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَعِدُّواْ لَهُمْ مَّا ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِّن قُوَّةٍ وَمِن رِّبَاطِ ٱلْخَيْلِ﴾ means the mares. Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us: Ibn Abī Yaḥyā related to us, tracing it back to the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Strength (al-quwwa) is shooting."
His saying: ﴿تُرْهِبُونَ بِهِ عَدْوَّ ٱللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ وَآخَرِينَ مِن دُونِهِمْ﴾: if you made it [وآخرين] accusative from His saying "and prepare for them, and for others besides them", it would be correct, as in His saying: ﴿والظالمين أَعَدَّ لهم عذابا أليما﴾. Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read: (ترهبون به عَدُوّاً لِلّهِ وعدوّكم), just as some read in [Sūrat] al-Ṣaff (كونوا أَنْصاراً لِلّهِ).

farraa:61-61.t: His saying: ﴿وَإِن جَنَحُواْ لِلسَّلْمِ فَٱجْنَحْ لَهَا...﴾: if you wish you make (لها) a pronoun referring to al-silm (peace), because it is feminine. If you wish you make it refer to the deed (al-faʿla), as He said ﴿إنّ رَبّكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, where only a verb was mentioned before it, so the hāʾ refers to the deed.

farraa:63-63.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَلَّفَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: between the hearts of the Anṣār, of al-Aws and al-Khazraj. There had been war between them, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered Medina, Allah set right relations between them through him and through Islam.
[Translator's note: the printed text has «أصح», evidently for «أصلح» ("set right").]

farraa:64-64.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ ٱللَّهُ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ﴾: the exegesis came as: Allah suffices you and suffices those who follow you. So the position of the kāf in (حسبك) is genitive (khafḍ), and (مَنْ) is in the position of the accusative according to the exegesis, as the poet said:
إذا كانت الهيجاء وانشقّتِ العصا * فحسبُك والضَّحاكَ سيفٌ مُهَنّد
(When war breaks out and the staff [of unity] is split, an Indian sword suffices you and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.)
It is not frequent in their speech to say حسبك وأخاك until they say حسبك وحسب أخيك; but we allowed it because in (حسبك) there is the sense of a verb acting [on an object], so we referred it back to the meaning of the kāf, not to its form, as in His saying ﴿إنَّا مُنَجُّوكَ وَأَهْلَكَ﴾, where He referred الأهل back to the meaning of the kāf.
If you wish, you make (مَنْ) in the position of the nominative, and that is the dearer of the two options to me, because the recitation points to the nominative sense; do you not see that He said: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:65-65.t: His saying: ﴿إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ﴾: the Prophet ﷺ used to send his Companions on campaigns on the basis that ten were for a hundred and one for ten, and so they were. Then it became hard for them that one should be matched against ten, so there was revealed: ﴿ٱلآنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوۤاْ أَلْفَيْنِ﴾.

farraa:66-66.t:
His saying: ﴿ٱلآنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضَعْفاً فَإِن يَكُنْ مِّنكُمْ مِّئَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُواْ مِئَتَيْنِ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوۤاْ أَلْفَيْنِ﴾: so Allah made clear their strength first and last. Al-Kisāʾī held this view and put (من) in the nominative.
[Translator's note: the last sentence appears to belong to the discussion of ﴿وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَكَ﴾ in verse 64; it is translated where the source places it.]

farraa:67-67.t: His saying: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَن يَكُونَ لَهُ أَسْرَىٰ﴾: its meaning is: it was not proper for him on the day of Badr to accept ransom for the captives ﴿حَتَّىٰ يُثْخِنَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾: until he prevails over many of those on the earth. Then there was revealed His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾.

farraa:68-68.t: His saying: ﴿لَّوْلاَ كِتَابٌ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾: concerning the ransom of the captives and the spoils. It has also been read (أَُسارى), and each is correct. And His saying (أَن يَّكُونَ) [is read] with the masculine and the feminine [يكون / تكون], like His saying (يَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ أَلْسِنَتهُم) and (تَشْهَدُ).

farraa:72-72.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, then He said: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَآءُ بَعْضٍ﴾: in inheritance. They used to inherit from one another to the exclusion of their relatives who had not emigrated.
That is His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُواْ مَا لَكُمْ مِّن وَلاَيَتِهِم﴾, meaning: of their inheritances.
Putting a kasra on the wāw in al-wilāya is more pleasing to me than a fatḥa, because it is mostly given a fatḥa when it has the meaning of support (nuṣra). Al-Kisāʾī used to read it with a fatḥa, taking it to mean support, and I do not think he knew the exegesis. For walītuhu wilāyatan (I took charge of it) they choose the kasra; but we have heard both, with fatḥa and kasra, in both their meanings. The poet said:
دعِيهمْ فَهُمْ أَلْبٌ عَلَىَّ وِلايةٌ * وحَفْرُهُمُ أَنْ يَعْلَموا ذاكَ دائب
(Leave them, for they are banded together against me in alliance, and their digging to find that out is unceasing.)
Then there was revealed afterwards: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ مَعَكُمْ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مِنكُمْ وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.

farraa:73-73.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾: if you do not inherit from one another on the basis of kinship, there will be discord. It is also mentioned that it concerns support: if you do not support one another, there will be discord.

farraa:75-75.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ مِن بَعْدُ وَهَاجَرُواْ وَجَاهَدُواْ مَعَكُمْ فَأُوْلَـٰئِكَ مِنكُمْ وَأْوْلُواْ ٱلأَرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَىٰ بِبَعْضٍ﴾: so they inherited from one another, and this latter verse abrogated the verse before it. That is that His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ تَفْعَلُوهُ تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾.
[Translator's note: the last sentence breaks off in the source; translated as it stands.]

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلأَنْفَالِ﴾: it was revealed concerning the spoils (anfāl) of the people of Badr. That is because when the Prophet ﷺ saw how few the people were and their dislike of fighting, he said: "Whoever kills a man shall have such-and-such, and whoever takes a captive shall have such-and-such."
When he had finished with the people of Badr, Saʿd ibn Muʿādh stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if you give these what you named for them, many of the Muslims will remain with nothing." So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, sent down: ﴿قُلِ ٱلأَنفَالُ للَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ﴾: he does with them what he wills. So they fell silent, with some dislike of that in their hearts.

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ﴾: this hāʾ is for the reinforcing (al-irdāf): Allah did not make the reinforcing ﴿إِلاَّ بُشْرَىٰ﴾.

farraa:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشِّيكُمُ ٱلنُّعَاسَ أَمَنَةً مِّنْهُ﴾: the Muslims spent the night of Badr without water, and they awoke in a state of major ritual impurity (janāba). Satan whispered to them, saying: "You claim that you are on the religion of Allah, yet you are without water while your enemy is at the water, and you pray in a state of janāba!" So Allah sent the sky upon them, and they drank and washed; and Allah removed from them the defilement (rijz) of Satan, meaning his whispering. They were in sand in which the feet sank, and the rain made it firm until men could tread firmly on it. That is His saying: ﴿وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ ٱلأَقْدَامَ﴾.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ أَنِّي مَعَكُمْ فَثَبِّتُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾: an angel would come to a man among the companions of Muhammad ﷺ and say: "I heard these people — meaning Abū Sufyān and his companions — saying: By Allah, if they charge at us, we shall be routed." Then the Muslims would tell one another of that, and their spirits would be strengthened. That is His inspiring the angels.
His saying: ﴿فَٱضْرِبُواْ فَوْقَ ٱلأَعْنَاقِ﴾: He taught them the places to strike, and said: strike the heads, the hands and the feet.
That is His saying: ﴿وَٱضْرِبُواْ مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ﴾.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾: He addressed the polytheists.
Then He said: ﴿وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾: (أَنّ) is accusative from two directions.
As for one of them: that is "because (بأن) the disbelievers have the punishment of the Fire"; the bāʾ was dropped and so it became accusative. The other accusative is that you imply a verb, as in the saying of the poet:
تسمع للأحشاء منه لغطا * ولليدين جُسْأَةً وبَدَدَا
(You hear a clamour from his insides, and [see] in his two forelegs stiffness and a wide stance.)
He implied (and you see in the two forelegs). Likewise He said ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾, and know ﴿َأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾. And if you wish you may make (أن) in the position of the nominative, meaning: ﴿ذٰلِكُمْ فَذُوقُوهُ﴾, and that is ﴿أَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ عَذَابَ ٱلنَّارِ﴾. Similar to it in the Book of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿خَتَمَ اللّهُ عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ وعَلَى سَمْعِهِمْ وعَلَى أَبْصَارِهِمْ غِشَاوَةً﴾: ʿĀṣim read it so, according to what al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to me; and he claimed that ʿĀṣim took it from him twice with the accusative [Translator's note: the source has "بانصب", a misprint for بالنصب]. And likewise His saying: ﴿وحُورٌ عِينٌ﴾.

farraa:16-16.t: His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مُتَحَرِّفاً لِّقِتَالٍ أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزاً إِلَىٰ فِئَةٍ﴾: it is an exception, and the one withdrawing (al-mutaḥayyiz) is other than مَن. And if you wish you may make it part of the description of مَن, and it is on the pattern of your saying: "except that he turns his back on them", meaning to return to the attack; as you say in speech: "عبدالله يأتيك إلاّ ماشيا" ("ʿAbdallāh will come to you, unless on foot") and "يأتيك إلا أن تمنعه الرحلة" ("he will come to you unless the journey prevents him"). And (إلا) here does not have the sense of His saying ﴿إلى طعام غيرَ ناظرين إنَاهُ﴾, because (غير) [there] follows the pattern of (لا), not the pattern of (إلا).

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿كَمَآ أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِن بَيْتِكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ despite their reluctance: so proceed with Allah's command concerning the spoils as you proceeded with your setting out while they were reluctant.
And it is said about it: they ask you about the spoils just as they disputed with you on the day of Badr and said: "You brought us out for booty and did not tell us of fighting so that we might prepare for it." That is His saying: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾

farraa:6-7.t:
His saying: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلْحَقِّ بَعْدَمَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾; and His saying: ﴿فاتَّقُوا الله وَأَصْلِحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾: He commanded the Muslims to share with one another in the spoils after they had been granted to them, as a command that is not obligatory.
His saying: ﴿وَإِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحْدَى ٱلطَّائِفَتِيْنِ﴾, then He said ﴿أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ﴾: He put (إحدى الطائفتين) in the accusative by "يعد", then repeated it, on the sense of: He promises you that one of the two parties is yours; as He said: ﴿فهل ينظرون إِلا الساعة﴾, then said: ﴿أَن تَأْتِيهم بغتة﴾: أن is in the position of the accusative just as الساعة was put in the accusative. And His saying: ﴿ولولا رِجال مؤمِنون ونِساء مؤمِنات﴾: He put them in the nominative by "لولا", then said: ﴿أَن تطئوهم﴾, so أن is in the position of the nominative by "لولا".

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿ بِأَلْفٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾, and it is read (مُرْدَفين). As for (مردِفين), it means following one another; and (مردَفين): it was done to them [i.e. they were made to follow].

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يسألونك عن الأنفال قل الأنفال لله والرسول﴾: resumptive speech with no grammatical position; يسألونك is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); عن الأنفال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يسألونك; قل is an imperative verb; الأنفال is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and لله is its khabar (predicate), and the nominal clause is in the position of an accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl); and الرسول is conjoined to الله.
﴿فاتقوا الله وأصلحوا ذات بينكم وأطيعوا الله ورسوله إن كنتم مؤمنين﴾: the ف is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; اتقوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi; أصلحوا is conjoined to اتقوا; ذات بينكم is the mafʿūl bihi; إن is conditional; كنتم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the ت is its noun and مؤمنين is its khabar; and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿إنما المؤمنون الذين إذا ذكر الله وجلت قلوبهم﴾: إنما is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; المؤمنون is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; الذين is the khabar (predicate); إذا is an adverb for what is future, containing the meaning of condition; the clause ذكر الله is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and الله is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and the clause وجلت قلوبهم has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
﴿وإذا تليت عليهم آياته زادتهم إيمانا﴾: conjunction [to] the first attribute; the clause زادتهم has no grammatical position; and إيمانًا is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), or a tamyīz (specification).
﴿وعلى ربهم يتوكلون﴾: a third attribute falling within the scope of the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative; على ربهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يتوكلون.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿الذين يقيمون الصلاة﴾: الذين is a badal (substitute); يقيمون الصلاة: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
﴿ومما رزقناهم ينفقون﴾: the و is a conjunction; مما: a preposition and its genitive noun; رزقناهم is a verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; and ينفقون is a verb and its fāʿil.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿أولئك هم المؤمنون حقا﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject); هم is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second khabar (predicate) [Translator's note: so in the source; on the second view هم would more usually be a second mubtadaʾ]; المؤمنون is the khabar in either case; the clause is the khabar of the demonstrative; and the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿حقًّا﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: they are the believers with a true belief (إيمانًا حقا); or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, emphasising the content of the clause, the implied form being: حق ذلك حقا.
﴿لهم درجات عند ربهم ومغفرة ورزق كريم﴾: لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar; درجات is the postponed mubtadaʾ; عند ربهم is an adverb attached to درجات, because it is in the sense of "rewards" (أجور), or attached to an omitted naʿt of درجات, because it is indefinite; and مغفرة ورزق كريم are conjoined to درجات.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿كما أخرجك ربك من بيتك بالحق﴾: ﴿كما﴾: the ك is a noun in the sense of مثل (like), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of a nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: this state — namely, their being removed from the assignment of the spoils (al-anfāl) — in their dislike of it, is like the state of your being brought out to war in their dislike of it; or their state in disliking what you saw fit of granting extra spoils to the fighters is like their state in disliking your going out to war. Or the ك is in the position of an accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e.: the spoils are established for Allah and for the Messenger ﷺ with an establishment like the establishment of your Lord's bringing you out of your house. ﴿ما﴾ is a maṣdar particle; ﴿أخرجك﴾ is a past verb, and the ك of address is a pronoun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿ربك﴾ is the fāʿil (agent); the clause ﴿أخرجك ربك﴾ is the ṣila of the maṣdar ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position; and the interpreted maṣdar from the maṣdar ﴿ما﴾ and the verb ﴿أخرج﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi, i.e.: كإخراج ربك إياك (like your Lord's bringing you out). ﴿من بيتك﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) أخرج; and ﴿بالحق﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: clothed with the truth (متلبسًا بالحق).
﴿وإن فريقا من المؤمنين لكارهون﴾: the و is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters); فريقًا is its noun; من المؤمنين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt; the ل is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); كارهون is the khabar of إن; and the clause is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the ك in أخرجك, i.e.: He brought you out in a state of their disliking it.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يجادلونك في الحق بعد ما تبين﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or a second ḥāl (circumstantial) of the ك, i.e.: He brought you out in the state of their disputing with you; or of the pronoun in كارهون, i.e.: averse in the state of disputing. في الحق is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يجادلونك; بعد is an adverb of time attached to يجادلونك; ما is maṣdariyya, and it and what falls in its scope are a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it, i.e.: after its becoming clear and its emergence.
﴿كأنما يساقون إلى الموت وهم ينظرون﴾: the clause is a ḥāl of the pronoun in ﴿لكارهون﴾, i.e.: in the state of their being likened to those who are driven to killing; كأنما is the restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa) particle; يساقون is an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive), and the و is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); إلى الموت is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يساقون; the و is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); and هم ينظرون is a clause in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وإذ يعدكم الله إحدى الطائفتين﴾: the و is resumptive; ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر or اذكروا (remember); the clause ﴿يعدكم الله﴾ is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; إحدى الطائفتين is the mafʿūl bihi; and an omitted element must be supposed, i.e.: victory over one of the two parties.
﴿أنها لكم وتودون أن غير ذات الشوكة تكون لكم﴾: ﴿أنها﴾: أن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters) and ﴿ها﴾ is the noun of أن; ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of أن; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أنها لكم﴾ is a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) for إحدى الطائفتين. تودون: the و is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), or a conjunction; تودون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn, and the و of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن غير ذات الشوكة...﴾ is the object of تودّون; the clause ﴿تكون﴾ is the khabar of أن; and ﴿لكم﴾ is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar of تكون.
﴿ويريد الله أن يحق الحق بكلماته ويقطع دابر الكافرين﴾: the و is a conjunction; يريد الله is a verb and its fāʿil; أن is maṣdariyya, and it with what falls in its scope is the object of يريد; بكلماته is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يحق; and ويقطع دابر الكافرين is a conjoined clause.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t: ﴿ليحق الحق ويبطل الباطل ولو كره المجرمون﴾: the ل is of causation (taʿlīl); يحق is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muḍmara) أن; and the ل with what falls in its scope is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted element, its implied form being: He did that in order to establish the truth and nullify falsehood.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿إذ تستغيثون ربكم﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative as a badal (substitute) for ﴿إذ﴾ in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وإذ يعدكم﴾; or in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر or اذكروا; or an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb ﴿يُحق﴾ in the previous ayah. The clause ﴿تستغيثون﴾ is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; تستغيثون is an imperfect verb, and the و of the plural is the fāʿil (agent); and ربكم is the object of تستغيثون.
﴿فاستجاب لكم أني ممدكم بألف من الملائكة مردفين﴾: the ف is a conjunction; لكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to استجاب; أن and what falls in its scope are in the position of an accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e.: يأتي ممدكم [Translator's note: so in the source; the intended paraphrase is evidently بأني ممدكم "with [the news] that I will reinforce you"], and the preposition and its genitive noun are likewise attached to استجاب; ممدكم is the khabar (predicate) of أن; بألف is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ممدكم; من الملائكة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ألف; مردفين is a second naʿt; and the object of مردفين is omitted, because it is an active participle, i.e.: others like them (أمثالهم).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿وما جعله الله إلا بشرى﴾: the و is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or the و is a conjunction to what precedes. ما is negative; جعله الله is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent), and the pronoun refers to the reinforcement; إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and بشرى is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), excepted.
﴿ولتطمئن به قلوبكم﴾: the و is a conjunction; the ل is of causation (taʿlīl); تطمئن is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after it, and أن with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the ل; the preposition and its genitive noun are conjoined to بشرى. The object of purpose is put in the genitive with the ل here because a condition for the accusative is missing, namely: identity of the agent. قلوبكم is the fāʿil of تطمئن.
﴿وما النصر إلا من عند الله﴾: the و is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or the و is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and the clause after it is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). ما is negative; النصر is the mubtadaʾ (subject); إلا is a particle of restriction; and من عند الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿إن الله عزيز حكيم﴾: the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl) of what precedes.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿إذ يغشيكم النعاس أمنة منه﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of an accusative as a second badal (substitute) for ﴿إذ﴾ in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وإذ يعدكم﴾, on the view that ﴿إذ تستغيثون﴾ is a badal; or in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر or اذكروا; or an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿النصر﴾ in the previous ayah. The clause ﴿يغشيكم النعاس﴾ is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; النعاس is the second object of يُغَشِّي; أمنة is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); and منه is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of أمنة.
﴿وينزل عليكم من السماء ماء ليطهركم به﴾: the و is a conjunction; ينزل is conjoined to يغشيكم; عليكم is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ينزل, and likewise ﴿من السماء﴾; ماء is the mafʿūl bihi. ليطهركم: the ل is of causation (taʿlīl), and يطهركم is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after it; the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb after it are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the genitive by the lām of causation, and the lām of causation and the interpreted maṣdar are attached to ﴿ينزل﴾; and به is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يطهركم.
﴿ويذهب عنكم رجز الشيطان﴾: the و is a conjunction; يذهب: an imperfect verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); عنكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يذهب; رجز: the mafʿūl bihi; and الشيطان: muḍāf ilayhi. The clause ﴿يذهب عنكم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ليطهركم﴾.
﴿وليربط على قلوبكم ويثبت به الأقدام﴾: the و is a conjunction; the ل is of causation; يربط: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of causation, and its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو); the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb after it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the genitive by the lām of causation, and the lām of causation and the interpreted maṣdar are attached to ﴿ينزل﴾; على قلوبكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يربط﴾; and the clause ﴿ليربط﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿ليطهركم﴾. يثبت: likewise conjoined to ﴿ليطهركم﴾; به: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يثبت﴾; and الأقدام: the mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إذ يوحي ربك إلى الملائكة أني معكم﴾: ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يثبت﴾, or an indeclinable noun in the position of an accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر (remember); and it is said: a third badal (substitute) for ﴿إذ﴾ in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وإذ يعدكم﴾, considering ﴿إذ﴾ in the previous ayah a second badal. The clause ﴿يوحي ربك﴾ is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; إلى الملائكة is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يوحي; أني and what falls in its scope are the object of يوحي; and معكم is an adverb attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of أني.
﴿فثبتوا الذين آمنوا﴾: the ف is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; الذين is the mafʿūl bihi; and the clause آمنوا has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
﴿سألقي في قلوب الذين كفروا الرعب﴾: the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; في قلوب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ألقي; الرعب is the mafʿūl bihi of ألقي; and the clause كفروا has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of the relative.
﴿فاضربوا فوق الأعناق واضربوا منهم كل بنان﴾: فاضربوا is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent); فوق is an adverb attached to اضربوا, and the mafʿūl bihi is omitted, i.e.: فاضربوهم فوق الأعناق; or ﴿فوق﴾ is a mafʿūl bihi by extension (ʿalā al-ittisāʿ).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ذلك بأنهم شاقوا الله ورسوله﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause شاقوا الله ورسوله is the khabar (predicate) of أن [Translator's note: the source does not state the khabar of the demonstrative; it is usually taken to be بأنهم…, i.e. the preposition and the interpreted maṣdar]; the Name of Majesty is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and رسوله is conjoined to it.
﴿ومن يشاقق الله ورسوله فإن الله شديد العقاب﴾: the و is resumptive; من is conditional, the mubtadaʾ; يشاقون [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah has يشاقق] is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the ف is linking; إن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), the Name of Majesty is its noun and شديد العقاب is its khabar; the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of ﴿من﴾; and the clause ﴿ومن يشاقق...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t: ﴿ذلكم فذوقوه وأن للكافرين عذاب النار﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: العقاب (the punishment); or the demonstrative is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: العقاب ذلكم; or it is in the position of an accusative on the basis of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb), as when you say: زيدًا فاضربه. The ف is resumptive, and what follows it is resumptive speech with no grammatical position; أن is conjoined to ذلكم; للكافرين is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted fronted khabar of ﴿أن﴾; and عذاب النار is its postponed noun.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a particle of the vocative; أي: the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative; ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أي﴾; آمنوا: a verb and its fāʿil (agent); and the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين, with no grammatical position.
﴿إذا لقيتم الذين كفروا زحفا فلا تولوهم الأدبار﴾: إذا is an adverb for future time, containing the meaning of condition; the clause لقيتم is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; الذين is its object; the clause كفروا is the ṣila of الذين, with no grammatical position; زحفًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of الذين, i.e.: in the state of their advancing; and it is said: ﴿زحفًا﴾ is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) by an omitted ḥāl, i.e.: زاحفين زحفًا (advancing an advance). The ف is linking; لا is prohibitive; تولوهم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the و is the fāʿil, and the ه is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and الأدبار: the second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿ومن يولهم يومئذ دبره﴾: the و is resumptive; من is conditional, the mubtadaʾ (subject); يولهم is a verb, a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent) and its first object; دبره is the second object of يولهم. ﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يولهم﴾; إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied sukūn, because the place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; and the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause.
﴿إلا متحرفا لقتال أو متحيزا إلى فئة﴾: إلا is a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr) because a prohibition precedes, and متحرفًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); or ﴿إلا﴾ is a particle of exception, and متحرفًا is excepted from the pronoun of the believers; لقتال is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿متحرفا﴾; and أو متحيزًا إلى فئة is conjoined to what precedes it.
﴿فقد باء بغضب من الله﴾: the ف links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the apodosis is joined with قد; باء: a past verb; بغضب is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to باء or to an omitted ḥāl; من الله is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective); and the clause is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis. The clause ﴿ومن يولهم...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿ومأواه جهنم وبئس المصير﴾: the و is resumptive and the clause after it is resumptive, with no grammatical position; or the و is a conjunction and the clause after it is conjoined. مأواه is the mubtadaʾ and جهنم is its khabar (predicate); بئس is a rigid (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; المصير is the fāʿil of بئس; and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bil-dhamm) is omitted, i.e.: مصيرهم (their destination).

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿فلم تقتلوهم ولكن الله قتلهم﴾: the ف is the faṣīḥa fāʾ; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive; تقتلوهم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم; the و is a particle of conjunction; لكن is an abrogating particle (inna and its sisters), الله is its noun, and the clause قتلهم is its khabar (predicate).
﴿وما رميت إذ رميت ولكن الله رمى﴾: conjoined to what precedes; ما is negative; ﴿إذ﴾ is an adverb for past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the negated verb ﴿رميت﴾; the second clause ﴿رميت﴾ is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the و is a conjunction; لكن is an abrogating particle, the Name of Majesty is its noun, and the clause رمى is its khabar.
﴿وليبلي المؤمنين منه بلاء حسنا﴾: the و is a conjunction; the ل is of causation (taʿlīl); يبلي is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن, and أن with what falls in its scope is in the position of a genitive by the ل; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being: فَعَلَ ذلك (He did that); المؤمنين is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); بلاء is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and حسنًا is a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿بلاء﴾, accusative.
﴿إن الله سميع عليم﴾: conjoined to what precedes; إن is an abrogating particle, the Name of Majesty is its noun, and سميع عليم are its two khabars.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t: ﴿ذلكم وأن الله موهن كيد الكافرين﴾: the demonstrative is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: ذلكم الإبلاء حق (that trial is true); أن and what falls in its scope are conjoined to ذلك; موهن is the khabar of ﴿أن﴾, and كيد الكافرين is muḍāf ilayhi. Or ﴿أن﴾ and what falls in its scope are conjoined to ﴿وليبلي﴾, or are in the position of an accusative by an implied verb, i.e.: واعلموا أن الله (and know that Allah).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿إن تستفتحوا فقد جاءكم الفتح﴾: إن is conditional; تستفتحوا is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the ف is linking because the apodosis is joined with قد; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq); and جاءكم الفتح is a verb, its mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and its fāʿil (agent).
﴿وإن تنتهوا فهو خير لكم﴾: conjoined to what precedes, and the i'rab is like what came before it; the apodosis is joined with the ف because it is a nominal clause made up of a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). The apodosis clause in both places is in the position of a jussive.
﴿وإن تعودوا نعد﴾: also conjoined, and the apodosis clause has no grammatical position.
﴿ولن تغني عنكم فئتكم شيئا ولو كثرت﴾: also conjoined; لن is for negation, the accusative and the future; تغني is accusative (manṣūb) by لن; عنكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تغني; فئتكم is the fāʿil of تغني and a muḍāf ilayhi; شيئًا is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is an attribute of the maṣdar, or a mafʿūl bihi; the و is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); لو is conditional; كثرت is the protasis; and the apodosis is omitted.
﴿وأن الله مع المؤمنين﴾: also conjoined; the hamza of ﴿أن﴾ has fatḥa by supposing the ل, the implied form being: ولأن الله مع المؤمنين (and because Allah is with the believers); the Name of Majesty is the noun of أن; and مع is an adverb of place attached to an omitted element, which is the khabar.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
